clue.text: Tried saving the wherewithal for pub, dishing

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held, 'Tried saving the wherewithal for pub, dishing', is an OCR garble: TRIED SAVING is clearly the anagram fodder, but whether 'pub, dishing' is 'publishing' (leaving no anagram indicator) or 'dishing' is the indicator (leaving 'the wherewithal for pub' as a nonsensical definition) cannot be settled without the printed page.
annotationWithheld.clue: Tried saving the wherewithal for pub, dishing

clue.text: Friendly but very noisy seaman splitting a drink

indicators.note: the two pieces split the drink apart by sitting in the middle of it

parts.note: ale is a drink, beer
ff (fortissimo) is the musical marking for very loud
AB is an able seaman

explanation.surface: A loud sailor barges in on someone's pint, though in a friendly enough way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'splitting' means the noisy seaman sits inside the drink, cutting it in two; 'a drink' is the usual crossword pint of beer.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe a person who is genial and easy to talk to.

clue.text: The opinions of wives change

indicators.note: to change is to alter the order, so the letters of wives are rearranged

explanation.surface: Wives' opinions shift over time.
explanation.definitionFit: Plural synonyms: a person's views are their beliefs or opinions.

clue.text: Not mounted without some added comment

parts.note: a rider is a clause or remark added to a statement or document
less can mean lacking, as in 'a year less a day'

explanation.surface: A horse is unmounted, and a speaker declines to add any comment.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse with nobody on its back is not mounted: no one is in the saddle.

clue.text: This country needs rain badly

indicators.note: something done badly is messed up, so the letters of rain are jumbled

explanation.surface: An arid nation is in desperate need of rainfall.
explanation.definitionFit: It is an example: a nation in the Middle East.

clue.text: The unit after being set about through blundering

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one, a single unit

indicators.note: the word for after is set around another piece, enclosing it

parts.note: next means coming after
per means through or by means of, as in 'per post'

explanation.surface: A unit, once its gear is set up, still performs ineptly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being set about' wraps the word for after around the word for through; 'The' is a link. 'set' tempts as a group of things, but it is part of the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone blundering lacks skill, which is what the adjective for an unskilled person conveys.

clue.text: Keep using a drug wrongly

indicators.note: letters put wrongly are out of place, so a drug is rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone holds on to their position by misusing medication.
explanation.definitionFit: As verbs, to keep and to protect both mean to watch over and preserve.

clue.text: Decide to clear up yet again

parts.note: re- is the prefix meaning again
to solve a mystery is to clear it up

explanation.surface: Someone decides to tidy things up one more time.
explanation.definitionFit: To make up one's mind firmly is a synonym of deciding.

clue.text: No-one left? That's good!

explanation.surface: Everyone's present and correct, so things are fine.
explanation.walkthrough: If no one is left (as opposed to right), everyone is on the right; the whole phrase is also an expression of approval.
explanation.definitionFit: Read literally, if nobody is on the left then everyone is on the other side; as an exclamation the phrase means satisfactory or fine.

clue.text: Just the bird for the picnic hamper!

definitions.text: Just the bird for the picnic hamper!

parts.words: Just the bird for the picnic hamper!
parts.note: the answer is a thrush whose name splits into words meaning open-country food, ideal outdoor eating

explanation.surface: Someone recommends a particular bird as ideal picnic food.
explanation.walkthrough: The bird's name reads as FIELD FARE: food eaten in a field, just what a picnic offers.
explanation.definitionFit: A winter-visiting thrush of Britain, whose name literally suggests food taken out in the fields.

clue.text: A giant collection of maps

explanation.surface: A huge compilation of maps.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth a Titan held up the sky; a bound book of maps is named after him.

clue.text: Possibly it robs the diner!

indicators.note: possibly signals one possible rearrangement of the letters of it robs

explanation.surface: A suspicious customer thinks a small restaurant is overcharging.
explanation.definitionFit: A small inexpensive restaurant is a diner, an eatery serving simple meals.

clue.text: Back number

parts.note: read as a thing that numbs the lower back: an anaesthetic injection given in the spine, often in childbirth

explanation.walkthrough: 'Back number' usually means an old issue of a magazine; here 'number' is something that numbs, used on the back.
explanation.definitionFit: A spinal anaesthetic deadens sensation below the waist, so it numbs the back and lower body.

clue.text: 20 a quarter, faces retirement

parts.note: E for East is one of the four quarters of the compass

indicators.note: retirement is a going back, so the word for faces is read backwards

parts.note: to face an opponent is to meet them

explanation.surface: A quarter of the team confronts the prospect of retiring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retirement' signals going backwards, turning the word for faces round. The definition is the answer to 20-down, a word for high regard.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean high regard or admiration for someone.

clue.text: Object about the right quartet doing well

indicators.note: the word for object goes about the other letters, enclosing them

parts.note: a thing is an object
IV is four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A thing involving a right-wing foursome is flourishing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' means the object surrounds the right quartet; IV for four is a Roman numeral, the usual crossword quartet.
explanation.definitionFit: Flourishing or prospering is to be doing well.

clue.text: Stop the meeting favouring a villain

parts.note: pro means in favour of
a rogue is a villain or scoundrel

explanation.surface: Someone sympathetic to a scoundrel halts proceedings.
explanation.walkthrough: To prorogue Parliament is to discontinue a session without dissolving it.
explanation.definitionFit: Suspending a session of Parliament or a council ends its sitting for a time.

clue.text: Land of Hope

parts.note: the fictional country created by the novelist Anthony Hope in The Prisoner of Zenda

explanation.walkthrough: 'Land of Hope' calls up 'Land of Hope and Glory', the patriotic British song; Hope here is the author Anthony Hope.
explanation.definitionFit: The imaginary Central European kingdom invented in an 1894 adventure novel by Anthony Hope.

clue.text: Rank appears material to a worker

parts.note: serge is a hard-wearing woollen fabric
a worker ant is the crossword's usual worker

explanation.surface: A position in the hierarchy seems relevant to an ordinary employee.
explanation.definitionFit: A non-commissioned officer's rank in the army or police.

clue.text: Fliers have to press in the self-starter

indicators.note: the word for press goes in among the other letters

parts.note: taken as written
to rush is to press forward or hurry

indicators.note: the starter of self is its opening letter

explanation.surface: Pilots must press the starter button.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starter' takes the first letter of self, and 'in' sets press inside the result. 'Fliers' suggests pilots, but here means birds.
explanation.definitionFit: Songbirds such as the song thrush are creatures that fly.

clue.text: Rate and mark as correct

explanation.surface: Scold someone and approve their work.
explanation.definitionFit: To rate is an old word for to scold, as does the phrasal verb; it also means to put a check mark beside an item.

clue.text: One who packs up what remains from the meteor

explanation.surface: A packer, and the hole left by a meteorite.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who puts goods into wooden boxes; also the bowl-shaped hollow left by an impact.

clue.text: Take into account 13

explanation.surface: Consider the earlier answer.
explanation.walkthrough: 13 refers to the answer to 13-across, a word for admiration.
explanation.definitionFit: To have regard for something is to take it into account; as a noun it means admiration, matching 13.

clue.text: About too old to get in, surance

parts.note: c (circa) means about, used with dates
over age means older than an allowed limit

explanation.surface: An elderly applicant is too old to qualify for an insurance policy.
explanation.definitionFit: Insurance gives protection against risk, so the amount of protection is a synonym.

clue.text: Stick with popular sculptor

parts.note: a rod is a stick
in means fashionable or popular

explanation.surface: Stick with a sculptor who is in fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: The French artist famous for The Thinker and The Kiss.

clue.text: The way a dispenser creates an impression

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a way
MPS stands for Member of the Pharmaceutical Society, a qualified dispensing chemist

explanation.surface: A dispensing machine leaves a mark in its distinctive manner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dispenser' looks like a machine but is a pharmacist, who dispenses medicine.
explanation.definitionFit: To press a mark into a surface is to make an imprint.

clue.text: Bohemian girl accepting a place in the US

indicators.note: the girl's name takes in another letter, accepting it inside

parts.note: Mimi is the heroine of Puccini's opera La Boheme

explanation.surface: An arty young woman admits she lives in an American city.
explanation.definitionFit: The Florida city is an American place.

clue.text: Set of books to give a man

parts.note: OT, the Old Testament, is a set of books of the Bible
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone hands a man some books.
explanation.definitionFit: A man's name, of German origin.

clue.text: Had a little blue gown edged with lace

indicators.note: only a little of the phrase gown edged is used, a run from its middle

explanation.surface: Someone owned a small blue dress trimmed with lace.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run from the end of 'gown' into the start of 'edged'.
explanation.definitionFit: To have possessed something is past ownership.

clue.text: Sap, making taunt about egghead, scoffed

indicators.note: turned about means the letters of taunt and E are shuffled

parts.note: the head of egg is its first letter, E
to scoff food is to eat it greedily

explanation.surface: Someone taunts an intellectual and mocks them, weakening their position.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges TAUNT plus E into ATTENU. 'Scoffed' sounds like mocked but means ate.
explanation.definitionFit: As verbs, to weaken or drain away strength gradually.

clue.text: Folk with a certain leaning for patriot

parts.note: a nation is a people, a folk
a stands for a certain one, as in 'a Mr Smith'
a list is a lean to one side, as a ship lists

explanation.surface: People with a particular bias claim to be patriots.
explanation.definitionFit: A strong supporter of one's own country and its independence.
